lines: - the brain stem consists of midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata
- it extends form posterior commissure to pyramidal decussation
- it gives rise to the cranial nerves (3-12)
- it gives rise to the oculomotor nerve (3) and the trochlear nerve (4)
- The midbrain has a narrow lumen called cerebral aqueduct (aqueduct of Sylvius).
which divides the midbrain into 2 divisions:
(1) superior and inferior colliculi: Mediates visual & auditory reflexes
(2) it gives rise to the oculomotor nerve (3) and the trochlear nerve (4)
which supply muscles of the eye
(3) Substantia nigra, the largest nucleus of midbrain
(3) Front pontine fibers: located most medially.
(1) Mesencephalic nucleus of the trigeminal nerve.
- it is a part of spinothalamic tract responsible for carrying sensation of
pain, temperature and crude touch from body below head
- it is a part of the auditory pathway responsible for hearing
Through its connection with the contralateral inferior colliculus of midbrain
- it is part of the dorsal column lemniscus pathway,
which important for somato-sensation as fine touch and pressure
- it is a part of trigeminal tract responsible for carrying sensation from face
- Red nucleus: - important for motor coordination through rubrospinal tract
- lateral lemniscus is not present at level of superior colliculus in midbrain
- the pons is connected with cerebellum through the middle cerebellar peduncles
- It contains the basilar groove that lodges the basilar artery .
- emerges from middle part of the pons
at its junction with the middle cerebellar peduncle.
- The abducent nerve (6), facial (7) and vestibulocochlear nerves (8):
- emerge at the lower border of the pons; between it and the medulla.
- it forms the upper part of the floor of the 4th ventricle.
- limitans sulcus: separates medial eminence from the upper vestibular area .
- a prominent elevation represents the lower part of medial eminence
- it is produced by the abducent nucleus surrounded by the facia nerve fibers.
- Medulla is connected with cerebellum through inferior cerebellar peduncles
- Pyramid: - it is formed by the corticospinal fibers before its decussation
- Olive: - it is formed by the olivary nuclei mainly the inferior olivary nucleus
- emerge between olive and inferior cerebellar peduncle
- it forms the lower part of the floor of the 4th ventricle.
- Gracile fasciculus: - its upper end expands to form gracile tubercle (nucleus)
- Cuneate fasciculus: - its upper end expands to form cuneate tubercle (nucleus)
- Vagal trigone: - overlies dorsal nucleus of vagus.
- it is part of the dorsal column lemniscus pathway,
which important for somato-sensation as fine touch and pressure
- gracile and cuneate tracts relay in gracile and cuneate nucli
- then the fibers cross to the opposite side as internal arcuate fibers,
- it is a part of spinothalamic tract responsible for carrying sensation of
pain, temperature and crude touch from body below head
carries proprioceptive sensation from the lower limb and trunk.
